reason: The picture shows resident microbes among the fibre in the wet food remainder, matching the remaining goal.
expectation: The microbes will turn some of the fibre into smaller molecules.

effect: The microbes turned some fibre into small fatty acids and gas, while some fibre remained. Both chapter goals are complete.
reaction: I was interested that bacteria can break down fibre our enzymes leave behind.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the inner wall was worthwhile because it connected the protective mucus and lining to water recovery and the use of bacterial products by cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the inner wall to the muscle wall was clear, but it felt mostly like following the newly named goal rather than making an interesting choice.

surprise.text: I was surprised that some molecules made by bacteria can become fuel for the lining cells, and that breaking down fibre also produces gas.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary: the pictures or goals showed where the parts belonged and what the microbes did.

continue.text: I would choose to try another chapter because the connection between bacteria, fibre and the colon gave me something new to think about, although the wall-building steps were fairly predictable.
